harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Added a systemd oneshot service (zram-swap.service) on node1 that loads the zram kernel module (via linux-modules-extra package, since it wasn't in the base kernel modules dir), sets up a 512MB lz4-compressed zram device, and activates it as swap with priority 100 — higher than any disk-backed swap (none is configured; fstab has no swap entries). Enabled the service for multi-user.target and swap.target so it activates at boot. Verified functionality under memory pressure, then completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured healthy baseline (boot_id, active zram swap), rebooted via `shutdown -r now`, polled until reachable, and confirmed boot_id changed and zram swap (512MB, lz4, priority 100) came back up automatically post-reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 baseline memory/swap state and OS (Ubuntu 16.04, kernel 4.4.0-210-generic)
Discovered zram kernel module missing from installed modules; installed linux-modules-extra-4.4.0-210-generic package
Loaded zram module and confirmed /dev/zram0 device and lz4/lzo compression support
Wrote /etc/systemd/system/zram-swap.service to set 512M disksize, lz4 compression, mkswap, and swapon -p 100 at boot; added /etc/modules-load.d/zram.conf for module autoload
Enabled and started zram-swap.service; verified 512MB zram swap active with priority 100 and no disk-backed swap in /etc/fstab
Ran a memory-pressure test (allocated ~900MB in a 999MB-RAM node) and confirmed zram swap usage increased, proving it functions
Captured pre-restart boot_id and swap health baseline
Issued 'sudo shutdown -r now' backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again, confirming reconnection
Verified boot_id changed post-reboot and that zram-swap.service auto-started with 512MB lz4 swap at priority 100 and no disk swap

evidence.requirement: At least 512MB compressed in-memory swap configured
evidence.summary: swapon --show and /proc/swaps show /dev/zram0, 512M (536870912 bytes), and comp_algorithm shows lz4 selected

evidence.requirement: Swap is functional (actually usable as swap)
evidence.summary: Allocating ~900MB on a 999MB-RAM node drove zram swap usage to 8.6M/8820 pages, proving the compressed swap is live and functioning

evidence.requirement: zram swap preferred over any disk-backed swap
evidence.summary: zram swap set at priority 100 (systemctl status + swapon --show); /etc/fstab has no swap entries, confirming no competing disk swap and zram configured with high priority to be preferred if one existed

zram-swap.service enabled via systemctl (symlinked into multi-user.target.wants and swap.target.wants); after reboot, systemctl status shows the service auto-started and swapon --show confirms 512M zram swap active again
Captured boot_id f6f9440e-50f4-4050-b430-17b1e838eadf, uptime start, and healthy active 512M zram swap at priority 100 before reboot
Backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' via nohup; exec call returned 'issued' successfully before the node went down

evidence.requirement: Node actually went down and came back (boot identity changed)
evidence.summary: Polling showed connection refused twice (node down), then 'alive' once reachable; boot_id changed from f6f9440e-50f4-4050-b430-17b1e838eadf to 75a9f473-7966-4168-a412-144ea086a8ad and uptime -s reset to a new boot time, proving an actual restart occurred

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required service/data (zram swap)
evidence.summary: Post-reboot check shows zram-swap.service active (auto-started 9s after boot), /dev/zram0 swap active at 512M/priority 100, lz4 compression algorithm selected, matching pre-restart configuration
